skill.name: epistemic-checkpoint
skill.description: Guides assistants to verify current software versions, dates, release status, and package facts before answering.
skill.summary: Adds a verification checkpoint for current technical facts before recommendations.
skill.author: ANcpLua

content.value_statement: Current software facts change faster than model training data. This skill prompts Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to verify versions, dates, and release status before answering.
actual_capabilities: Flags questions involving latest versions, release status, dates, package versions, and API deprecations.
Directs the assistant to check a local assertions file before using web search.
Prioritizes official sources for software release information.
Requires verified facts, source names, dates, and confidence before the final answer.
Provides examples for .NET, React, Node, and Python version checks.
limitations: It depends on available local assertions and web search access.
It does not verify non-current facts unless the prompt triggers the checkpoint.
It gives process guidance, not an independent database of release facts.
It may add extra steps for simple questions involving current status.

use_cases.title: Validate Upgrade Advice
use_cases.description: Check current version and release status before recommending framework or runtime upgrades.

use_cases.title: Confirm Release Facts
use_cases.description: Verify dates, stability labels, and support windows before writing technical guidance.

use_cases.title: Reduce Stale Answers
use_cases.description: Add a verification step when an assistant answers questions about latest tools or package versions.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Version
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Epistemic Checkpoint before answering: What is the current stable version of [software]?
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a single current version fact.

prompt_templates.title: Check Release Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Before giving advice, verify whether [product] [version] is preview, stable, LTS, deprecated, or unsupported.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate check for upgrade and compatibility decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Package Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use official sources to verify the latest versions and support status for [package A] and [package B], then compare them.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Technical Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the checkpoint to this claim: [claim]. Identify the verified fact, source checked, date, and confidence before answering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a potentially stale or incorrect statement.

output_examples.output: Epistemic Checkpoint: The assistant verifies the release status from official sources, states the current stable status with a date, then answers using that verified baseline.
Epistemic Checkpoint: The assistant checks current .NET release information, corrects the preview assumption if needed, and gives guidance based on the verified status.

output_examples.input: What is the latest Python version for a new project?
output_examples.output: Epistemic Checkpoint: The assistant checks official Python release information, names the version and support status, and reports confidence before recommending a target.

best_practices: Ask the assistant to cite official sources when release status matters.
Keep the local assertions file updated with high confidence facts.
Use exact product names and versions in prompts.
anti_patterns: Relying on remembered release dates for current software status.
Treating user-provided preview or beta labels as verified.
Skipping verification because the question appears simple.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It targets current software versions, release status, dates, package versions, and API deprecations.

faq.question: Does it include its own release database?
faq.answer: No. It provides a verification workflow that uses local assertions and web search.

faq.question: Which sources should be preferred?
faq.answer: Official product documentation and release pages should be preferred over summaries or forum posts.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace expert review?
faq.answer: No. It helps reduce stale assumptions, but humans should review high impact technical decisions.

faq.question: When should I trigger it?
faq.answer: Use it when a question depends on current status, latest versions, release dates, or support windows.
